subject: Recap + next steps: multi-tool calling & fallback patterns for FinEdge
messages:

Subject: Recap + next steps: multi-tool calling & fallback patterns for FinEdge

Hi Jenna / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical follow-up:

Call highlights
- Goal: embed Redwood for FinEdge’s customer-support assistant (high-QA, low-latency) and add structured tool calls for payments and account lookups.
- Constraints: PII on customer payment history (needs strict residency), 99th %-ile latency target <= 450ms for API-based flows, budget sensitivity for per-token costs.

Proposed integration approach (high-level)
1) SDK & auth
   - Use the Redwood server SDK (node/python) for all tool-invocation logic to keep API keys out of the browser.
   - OAuth for end-user flows where FinEdge needs to act on behalf of the user (payment initiation); API keys for backend-to-backend calls.
2) Routing & fallbacks
   - Region-aware routing (US primary, EU fallback).
   - Model variant fallback: fast quantized variant for latency-sensitive UI calls, higher-quality variant for long-form decisions.
3) Tool / function calling patterns
   - Define a small canonical tool set (account_lookup, initiate_payment, knowledge_search).
   - Use parallel fan-out for non-mutating tools (knowledge_search, enrichment) and sequential/controlled calls for mutating ops (initiate_payment).
   - Error handling: optimistic UX + graceful degradation (e.g., show cached account view when account_lookup fails; queue payment for manual review if payment service returns transient error).
4) Embeddings & rerankers
   - Index customer docs and KB with an ANN (FAISS/Annoy) for retrieval. Use a lightweight embedding model for indexing and a stronger reranker (cross-encoder) at top-K to preserve QA quality.

Attachments: I attached a short patterns doc (redwood-multitool-patterns-v1.pdf) and a proposed mutual action plan (FinEdge-MAP.xlsx).

Next steps
- Internal technical working session: propose Tue/Wed next week (Jun 16/17). Karthik and Marcus from our infra team to join.
- Jenna: please confirm whether payments access will be via a service account or if FinEdge requires user-scoped OAuth.

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,

1) Data residency: we have to keep payment transaction metadata in our EU tenant for EU customers. Would you recommend Redwood Private in-region or can Hosted with regional routing satisfy audit requirements?

2) Latency: if we do parallel fan-out for KB + enrichment, what are the typical tail-latency tradeoffs you see? We worry about the UX if anything waits for cross-encoder reranking.

4) Reranker choices: cross-encoder sounds expensive. Any recommended shortlist (open models) that balance cost/quality?

Great questions — quick answers and what we'll cover in the tech session:

1) Data residency
   - Recommendation: Redwood Private (VPC in eu-west1) for EU-payment metadata to satisfy audit/residency; hosted + regional routing covers latency but not strict residency requirements unless contractualized. We can scope Private for only the payment index if you want a hybrid approach.

2) Latency & parallel fan-out
   - Fan-out pattern: run lightweight retrieval + enrichment in parallel (embedding search, entity enrichment), then run cross-encoder only on top-N (N=5) to minimize tail. Typical added tail for cross-encoder rerank is 80–200ms depending on model. If 99th %-ile matters, do cross-encoder asynchronously (show preliminary answer, update with reranked result when ready) or use a cheaper symmetric reranker for strict SLOs.

3) Embedding storage
   - You can host the vector store in your GCP project (we integrate with custom Annoy/FAISS endpoints) or use Redwood-managed index with VPC peering. Hosting yourself gives you full control over residency.

4) Reranker shortlist (open models)
   - Distil-cross-encoder-base (fast, decent quality)
   - miniLM-cross (balanced)
   - For highest quality: cross-encoder-large (higher cost) — we recommend the cascade pattern (embed -> ANN -> cross-encoder).

Proposed agenda for the Wed technical session (Jun 17, 9:00am PT):
- Walk through sample SDK call flow for tool-calling (server-side orchestration + client shim)
- Auth options and sample OAuth flows (SSO requirements mapping)
- Routing & model fallback policies (policy examples + precedence)
- Failure modes and user experience: retries/backoff, cached fallback, operator alerting

I added Karthik to this thread; he'll bring an example implementation and a short runbook. Jordan will take notes and draft the follow-up plan.

If Wed 9am PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite.
